title: Microsoft extends multiyear, multibillion-dollar partnership with OpenAI
content: Microsoft announced the third phase of its long-term partnership with OpenAI through a multiyear, multibillion-dollar investment to accelerate AI breakthroughs. Azure remains OpenAI's exclusive cloud provider, and Microsoft will deploy OpenAI models across its consumer and enterprise products.

title: OpenAI raises $6.6 billion led by Thrive Capital
content: OpenAI closed a $6.6 billion funding round at a $157 billion valuation led by Thrive Capital with participation from Microsoft, Nvidia, SoftBank and Khosla Ventures. The company said the funding will strengthen its leadership in frontier AI research and expand compute capacity. ChatGPT now has more than 250 million weekly active users, showing strong growth.

title: OpenAI announces $40 billion financing led by SoftBank
content: OpenAI announced new funding of $40 billion at a $300 billion post-money valuation, led by SoftBank, to push the frontier of AI research and scale compute infrastructure. It is the largest private technology funding round on record.

title: OpenAI to acquire io, the AI device startup from Jony Ive
content: OpenAI agreed to acquire io, the hardware startup co-founded by Jony Ive, in an all-stock deal valued at about $6.5 billion. The io team will merge with OpenAI to build a new family of AI-native devices.

title: Amazon completes $4 billion investment in Anthropic
content: Amazon completed its $4 billion investment in Anthropic, making AWS Anthropic's primary cloud provider for mission-critical workloads. Anthropic will use AWS Trainium and Inferentia chips to build and train future foundation models, and Claude is available to AWS customers via Amazon Bedrock. The partnership reflects strong enterprise demand.

title: Anthropic raises $13 billion Series F led by ICONIQ
content: Anthropic raised $13 billion in a Series F round at a $183 billion post-money valuation led by ICONIQ, co-led by Fidelity and Lightspeed Venture Partners. The company reported rapid revenue growth driven by enterprise adoption of Claude and Claude Code, and said the funds will expand capacity and international expansion.

title: Google invests in Anthropic and expands cloud partnership
content: Google invested about $300 million in AI startup Anthropic, taking a roughly 10% stake, and Anthropic selected Google Cloud as a preferred cloud provider for training its Claude models.

title: Mistral AI raises €1.7 billion Series C led by ASML
content: French AI startup Mistral AI raised €1.7 billion in a Series C round led by semiconductor equipment maker ASML, valuing the company at €11.7 billion. Existing investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed, General Catalyst, Index Ventures and Nvidia participated. The deal creates a strategic partnership to use AI across ASML's products.

title: Mistral AI raises €600 million Series B led by General Catalyst
content: Mistral AI raised €600 million in equity and debt in a Series B round led by General Catalyst, valuing the Paris-based startup at about $6 billion. The company has grown quickly by releasing efficient open-weight models and enterprise offerings.

title: Cohere raises $500 million to expand enterprise AI
content: Toronto-based Cohere raised $500 million in a Series D round valuing it at $5.5 billion, with backing from Nvidia, Salesforce Ventures, Cisco and AMD. Cohere focuses on secure, private enterprise AI deployments and retrieval-augmented generation.

title: xAI raises $6 billion Series C
content: Elon Musk's xAI raised $6 billion in a Series C round from investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia Capital, Fidelity, Nvidia and AMD, to expand its Colossus supercomputer and accelerate Grok model development.

title: Perplexity raises $500 million at $9 billion valuation
content: AI search startup Perplexity raised $500 million led by IVP at a $9 billion valuation as queries on its answer engine grew rapidly. Perplexity is challenging Google in search with cited AI answers, though it also faces copyright lawsuits from publishers.

title: Google signs licensing deal with Character.AI, hires founders
content: Google agreed to license Character.AI's large language models and rehired co-founders Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas into Google DeepMind. Character.AI will continue to operate its consumer product with a smaller team, raising concerns about the startup's future growth.

title: Microsoft hires Inflection AI founders and licenses its models
content: Microsoft hired Inflection AI co-founders Mustafa Suleyman and Karen Simonyan along with most of the startup's staff to form Microsoft AI, and paid about $650 million to license Inflection's models. Inflection pivoted toward enterprise AI, a setback after its high-profile consumer launch.

title: Safe Superintelligence raises $1 billion
content: Safe Superintelligence, the AI lab co-founded by former OpenAI chief scientist Ilya Sutskever, raised $1 billion from Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia Capital, DST Global and SV Angel to develop safe AI systems.

title: Thinking Machines Lab raises record $2 billion seed round
content: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab raised a $2 billion seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz at a $12 billion valuation, with Nvidia, Accel, AMD and Cisco participating. It is among the largest seed rounds ever, reflecting strong investor appetite for frontier AI talent.

title: Hugging Face raises $235 million Series D from tech giants
content: Hugging Face raised $235 million in a Series D round led by Salesforce Ventures with participation from Google, Amazon, Nvidia, Intel, AMD, Qualcomm and IBM, valuing the open-source AI platform at $4.5 billion.

title: Hugging Face acquires humanoid robotics startup Pollen Robotics
content: Hugging Face acquired Pollen Robotics, the French maker of the Reachy 2 humanoid robot, to expand its open-source robotics efforts and sell robots to researchers.

title: Meta invests $14.3 billion in Scale AI
content: Meta invested about $14.3 billion for a 49% stake in Scale AI, and Scale founder Alexandr Wang joined Meta to lead a new superintelligence group. Several Scale customers including Google and OpenAI reportedly paused work with the data-labeling company afterward.

title: Databricks raises $10 billion Series J led by Thrive Capital
content: Databricks raised $10 billion in Series J funding at a $62 billion valuation led by Thrive Capital, with Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global, GIC, Insight Partners and WCM. The company expects strong revenue growth driven by its data intelligence platform and AI products.

title: Databricks acquires MosaicML for $1.3 billion
content: Databricks agreed to acquire generative AI startup MosaicML for about $1.3 billion to help enterprises build and train their own large language models on the Databricks lakehouse.

title: Nvidia completes acquisition of Run:ai
content: Nvidia completed its roughly $700 million acquisition of Israeli GPU orchestration startup Run:ai after regulatory approval, and said it will open-source the Run:ai software.

title: Stability AI faces leadership turmoil as CEO Emad Mostaque resigns
content: Stability AI CEO Emad Mostaque resigned amid investor pressure, cash burn concerns and the departure of key researchers. The company later raised new capital and restructured, but faces lawsuits over training data and declining market share.

title: Runway raises $308 million Series D led by General Atlantic
content: Generative video startup Runway raised $308 million in a Series D round led by General Atlantic with Fidelity, Nvidia and SoftBank participating. Runway launched its Gen-4 video model and is expanding its film and animation studio, showing strong growth with media customers.

title: Figure AI raises $675 million from Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon and OpenAI fund
content: Humanoid robot developer Figure AI raised $675 million in a Series B round at a $2.6 billion valuation from Microsoft, the OpenAI Startup Fund, Nvidia, Jeff Bezos' Bezos Expeditions and Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund. Figure also entered a collaboration with OpenAI on AI models for humanoid robots.

title: Roboflow raises $40 million Series B led by GV
content: Computer vision platform Roboflow raised a $40 million Series B led by GV, with Craft Ventures and Y Combinator participating. Over a million developers use Roboflow to build vision models, and the company is seeing strong growth in enterprise adoption for manufacturing and logistics.

title: Twelve Labs raises $50 million Series A for video understanding
content: Twelve Labs, which builds multimodal foundation models for video understanding, raised a $50 million Series A co-led by New Enterprise Associates and NVentures, Nvidia's venture arm. The startup will grow its research team and expand its developer platform.

title: Encord raises $30 million Series B for multimodal data development
content: London-based Encord raised a $30 million Series B led by Next47 to expand its data development platform for computer vision and multimodal AI. The YC alum reported strong growth with customers in healthcare, robotics and autonomous vehicles.

title: Encord raises $60 million Series C led by Wellington Management
content: Encord raised a $60 million Series C led by Wellington Management to build data infrastructure for physical AI, robotics and multimodal models, after growing revenue rapidly over the past year.

title: Voxel51 raises $30 million Series B led by Bessemer
content: Voxel51, maker of the FiftyOne open-source computer vision toolkit, raised a $30 million Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners to expand its enterprise platform for visual AI data curation.

title: Clarifai cuts staff amid competitive computer vision market
content: Clarifai reportedly reduced headcount as competition intensified in computer vision platforms and customers shifted spending toward large language models. The company said it remains focused on its full-stack AI platform.

title: Foundation model market landscape 2025
content: The foundation model market is concentrated among a few frontier labs: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind lead on capability, with xAI and Meta close behind. Mistral AI leads in Europe with open-weight models, while Cohere targets private enterprise deployments. Funding has concentrated in mega-rounds backed by hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google) and chipmakers (Nvidia), creating strong growth but heavy compute dependency.

title: Computer vision startup funding report 2024-2025
content: Computer vision startups saw renewed investor interest in 2024 and 2025 driven by multimodal models, robotics and physical AI. Data-centric tooling companies such as Encord, Voxel51 and Roboflow raised Series B rounds, while video understanding (Twelve Labs) attracted strategic investors like Nvidia. Older platforms such as Clarifai faced pressure from foundation models that perform vision tasks out of the box.

title: Investor activity in AI startups
content: Nvidia, Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed, Sequoia and Salesforce Ventures were among the most active investors in AI startups by number of deals, while hyperscalers Microsoft, Amazon and Google wrote the largest checks. Corporate investors increasingly pair investment with cloud and chip commitments.

title: Humanoid robotics and embodied AI outlook
content: Humanoid robotics companies such as Figure AI raised large rounds as vision-language-action models improved. Tesla is developing Optimus, and open-source efforts like Hugging Face's acquisition of Pollen Robotics aim to democratize robotics research. Investors see strong long-term growth but significant commercialization risk.
